title: chenopodium ambrosioides subsp. suffruticosum
intro: Chenopodium ambrosioides subsp. suffruticosum, commonly known as Mexican tea or epazote, is a plant species belonging to the Amaranthaceae family. It has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, which include treating digestive issues such as nausea, flatulence, and bloating, as well as its antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties. The therapeutic actions of Mexican tea include carminative, antiemetic, and antispasmodic effects, which contribute to its use in alleviating symptoms of indigestion and other gastrointestinal problems. The bioactive constituents of Chenopodium ambrosioides subsp. suffruticosum include volatile oils, flavonoids, and alkaloids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and have been studied for their potential health benefits.
